what_it_does: When an AI model is launched from scratch — for example, in cloud spot-computing or on an edge device — it can take a surprisingly long time before the GPU actually starts doing useful math. A big part of that delay comes from loading pre-compiled GPU programs (called kernels — each one is a small piece of code the GPU runs for a specific operation like a convolution or a matrix multiply) from a library into the GPU's memory before they can execute. PASK attacks this 'cold-start' problem by loading those GPU programs in advance and in parallel with other work, instead of waiting until the last moment, and by keeping a catalog of already-loaded programs so later layers of the network can reuse them instead of reloading. The result is that models reach full speed faster, which matters whenever a serving system frequently spins up fresh model instances.
